1g and l, substituted ortho-carbonylphenoxyacetamides, were identified as potent inhibitors of HIF transcriptional activation and Hsp60 chapperone activity.
a series of ortho-carborylphenoxyacetamides were synthesized and their ability to block HIF-1 activity and inhibit HIF-1 accumulation was evaluated.

the ortho-carboranes substituted at the 2-position of the phenoxy moiety with an acetamido group at the 4-position of the phenyl moiety showed significant inhibition of HIF-1 activity and Hsp60 activity.

the design and synthesis of a series of novel ortho-carboranylated HIF-1 inhibitors.
the development of novel ortho-carboranylated HIF inhibitors that may serve as lead compounds for the development of new anticancer drugs.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of ortho-carbonylphenoxyacetamides as potential HIF-1 inhibitors.

compound 1g and l are potent and selective HIF-1 inhibitors and may be useful as lead compounds for further development of novel HIF inhibitors.
the carborane substituent at the ortho position of the phenyl group is an essential moiety for HIF-1 inhibition.
the introduction of ortho-carbon substituents into the phenoxyacetanillides led to the development of novel HIF-1 inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ortho-carboranes are promising candidates for HIF-1 inhibitors and that the ortho-carboranophenoxy moiety is an important structural component for HIF-α inhibitors.
the ortho-carboranes are a promising new scaffold for the development of HIF-1 inhibitors.
ortho-carboranes can be used as scaffolds in HIF-1 inhibitors.

the introduction of an ortho-carboranylpheoxyl moiety into an Hsp90 inhibitor can lead to a compound with dual HIF-1 inhibitory activity and Hsp90 inhibitory activity.
the ortho-carboranyloxyacetanilide derivatives are a novel class of HIF-1 inhibitors with potential utility as anticancer drugs.
the introduction of ortho-carbonate substituents to the phenoxyacetanilate core structure is an efficient strategy for the development of potent HIF-1 inhibitors.
